install_script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /workspace/TsLightRAG
# Image prerequisites: Node 24.19.0, npm 11.9.0, Python 3.12, make and a C++ compiler.
test "$(node --version)" = v24.19.0
test "$(npm --version)" = 11.9.0
mkdir -p .cache/node-gyp .tools
npm_config_devdir="$PWD/.cache/node-gyp" npm ci
npm run build
# Independent source references are development validation tools, never application services.
reference_dir="$PWD/.tools/LightRAG-upstream"
reference_pin=aaebfe1bb8d55deb6a4304d357a3bf4c92fcd40a
if [ ! -e "$reference_dir" ]; then
  git clone --no-checkout https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG.git "$reference_dir"
  git -C "$reference_dir" checkout --detach "$reference_pin"
fi
test "$(git -C "$reference_dir" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$reference_pin"
git -C "$reference_dir" diff --quiet HEAD -- lightrag
python3 -m pip install --upgrade --cache-dir .cache/pip --target .tools/reference-python -r scripts/reference/requirements.txt
npm run test:reference
start_skill:
Use the existing /workspace/TsLightRAG checkout; each task is isolated. Do not create a Git worktree unless explicitly requested. Preserve user changes. During dependency setup, keep tracked source/manifests/lockfiles unchanged; implement code changes only within the user's coding task scope.

The snapshot retains dependencies, dist, ignored reference source and verification tools, but not processes. Rebuild after source changes or missing dist with npm run build. From the repository root, start npm start -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9621 --data-dir ./data in a managed terminal, capturing logs in .tools/server.log if needed. Preserve existing ./data and never remove snapshots or lock files to solve startup failures. Stop only processes owned by the task; a second writer using that data directory must fail.

Readiness: locally fetch /, /graph, /api/v1/health and /api/v1/parsers/capabilities. Expect HTML root, health.status ok, storage.status ready, jobs.available true and nine supported formats. Current stage is S11. Missing query/embedding model profiles produce usable false and are an expected unconfigured state, not proof that actual indexing/answering works. Validate real workflows with isolated fixtures and the existing browser suite. Do not create localhost preview links.

For development, stop the task-owned production server occupying 9621, then npm run dev starts the watched server on 9621 and Vite on 5174. Fetch the health API through the Vite proxy and a transformed source module, then stop the task-owned concurrently supervisor with SIGTERM and verify both ports stop before production restart. Capture and retain that supervisor PID when starting development. In this runner, interrupting the outer managed terminal can terminate its wrapper without forwarding the signal to the supervisor; the tested fallback is SIGTERM to the exact task-owned concurrently PID, which closes both children. Do not use broad pkill or stop an unrelated process to free a port.

Validation commands from the root: npm run typecheck; npm run lint; npm run test:unit; npm run test:protocol; npm run test:integration; npm run test:coverage; npm run test:e2e; npm run test:reference. Test scripts build first, so do not run their builds concurrently. Core coverage gates are 85% lines and 80% branches for storage/indexing/retrieval. Chromium at /usr/bin/chromium is selected by the Playwright config. Basic suites need no real model key. Reference regeneration is required when claiming G01-G12 acceptance, and is separate from application runtime; setup is documented in scripts/reference/README.md and retained by the install script. The reference runner requires the exact pinned upstream SHA, reproduces five stored fixtures and must fail on an unexplained difference; do not silently rewrite expectations to pass.

Model configuration belongs in /settings/models and the local protected data directory; no business environment variables or external database are required. Query and embedding are required for real model workflows; rerank is optional. Never put credentials in chat, logs, setup scripts or repository files. Provider destinations depend on user choice and may require environment network settings. Current-instance validation, saved draft, user publication and fresh-task restoration are separate statuses. See docs/VALIDATION_REPORT.md and docs/reference/s11-validation.json for tested scope, declared upstream adaptations and unrun external checks. S12 license/documentation/delivery review remains separate.
productionAndDevelopment: locally verified; development supervisor SIGTERM closes both children
